task_name: the payload type and the client call in `web/`

rubric.result: The objective promises three things: web/ asks for the coverage of every clone, with its own declared types, and with the error handling the other calls already have. All three are in the diff. web/src/api/client.ts:23-26 adds `fetchCoverage(signal?)` that calls `request<{ coverage: RepoCoverage[] }>('/api/coverage', { signal })` and returns `body.coverage`; the types are declared in web/src/api/types.ts:109-121 and imported from './types', never from server/; the error handling is the shared `request` helper, so a non-ok response arrives as an `ApiError` carrying the server's `code`, which the second new test pins. Nothing beyond the objective is implemented.

Both tests the **TDD:** line names exist with the literal names asked for. `test('fetchCoverage reads the coverage array of the envelope')` (client.test.ts:110-128) stubs fetch with `stubResponse({ coverage })` and asserts `expect(result).toEqual(coverage)` plus the requested URL '/api/coverage' — the envelope's array, over a stubbed fetch, as written. `test('fetchCoverage turns an error envelope into an ApiError with its code')` (client.test.ts:130-140) asserts `toBeInstanceOf(ApiError)` and `(error as ApiError).code` is 'internal'; it asserts the code and not the HTTP status, and `stubResponse` carries no `status` field at all, so the assertion can only be satisfied by reading the envelope. Same input, same expected value as the plan wrote down.

The Contract block for web/src/api/types.ts is reproduced name by name: `CoverageFormat` = 'istanbul' | 'lcov' | 'cobertura'; `CoverageState` = 'measured' | 'no-artifact' | 'unreadable-artifact'; `RepoCoverage` with `id: string`, `state: CoverageState`, `percentage: number | null`, `lines: { covered: number; total: number } | null`, `source: CoverageFormat | null`, `measuredAt: string | null` — same names, same order, same nullability, all exported. Against the Current state block, `fetchCoverage(signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<RepoCoverage[]>` sits directly beside `fetchRepos`, reads '/api/coverage' through the same `request` helper and answers `body.coverage`, so the error path is the one `ApiError` already gives. No symbol states anything else.

Rows this diff bears on: Route — `GET /api/coverage` with body `{ coverage: [...] }` like `/repos`, implemented as `request<{ coverage: RepoCoverage[] }>('/api/coverage')`, the exact mirror of the `{ repos }` call above it. Formats — exactly three members in `CoverageFormat`, no fourth, JaCoCo absent. Metric lines only — `lines: { covered, total }` and `percentage`, no other counter. `No candidate counts` and `Artefact that is not its format` — both states present in `CoverageState`, with every value nullable so `no-artifact` can carry all-null. Measure date ISO 8601 — `measuredAt: string | null`, and the test uses '2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z'. Spanish only for UI copy — every identifier, comment and test name in this diff is English. Rows about `server/src/coverage/`, the candidate order, the cache key and the ranking order have no subject in this diff and are untouched. No row is implemented with a different value.

Exemplars: web/src/api/types.ts is itself an exemplar of the plan and the new declarations follow its idiom exactly — closed string unions above the interface they classify, one short doc line per payload entry, mirroring `Clone` ('One entry of `GET /repos`. No author identity: only counts and dates.'). `fetchCoverage` follows the shape of `fetchRepos` line for line. Repo rules (AGENTS.md), all of which bind because none of ct's five documents speaks about them: code in English (met), Vitest tests beside the code (met, client.test.ts), relative imports with no `.js` suffix in web/ (met: './client', './types'), web/ never imports from server/ (met: only './types'), author names and emails never leave the server (met: `RepoCoverage` declares no author field, and the diff's own comment says so). conventions/style.md, rule by rule: the two host files are pre-existing non-conforming modules (prose docstrings throughout types.ts and client.ts, and every function at module level). The declared-debt exemption applies here and not the born-conforming clause: `RepoCoverage` is one more payload contract in the file whose declared purpose is payload contracts, and `fetchCoverage` is one more endpoint call beside four others — both genuinely extend what was already there, and the brief's **Files:** fixes both hosts, so the doc comment at types.ts:113 and the module-level `export async function` at client.ts:23 follow the style of their host and are not findings. Identifiers are English. conventions/architecture.md: no new module, no layer crossed; the boundary rule that applies is that payload types are declared on this side, which is what the diff does. conventions/decisions.md: the payload contract now exists on both sides of a process boundary, which is the unavoidable copy the document allows; the brief declares it and points at Task 5's assertion on the literal payload as the test that compares the two, so it is declared and measured, not implicit. conventions/testing.md: names are sentences, the assertion is on the literal payload the endpoint returns and on the URL requested, no mother is needed for a payload literal, and `stubResponse` was already there. conventions/defects.md, one verdict per rule: (1) closed vocabulary — conforming: `CoverageFormat` and `CoverageState` are closed unions and the absent states ('no-artifact', 'unreadable-artifact') are members of the vocabulary rather than optionals; this diff dispatches over neither, so there is no catch-all to look for. (2) raw map as the return value of logic — no subject: `fetchCoverage` returns `RepoCoverage[]`, a declared type; the `{ coverage: RepoCoverage[] }` envelope is the shape of the wire read once at the boundary and immediately projected. (3) two fields that have to agree — no sentinel: absence travels as `null` inside the type, never as 0 % or an empty string, which is exactly what the desired end state demands. `state` and the nullability of `percentage` do restate each other, and a discriminated union would make the disagreement unrepresentable, but that shape is the brief's Contract block and a row of the closed decisions table ('No candidate counts | state `no-artifact`, every value `null`'), so the diff could not have been written any other way and this is not counted as a finding. (4) an error named for what happens — conforming: the only error is the pre-existing `ApiError`, named for the failure and carrying `code`; the diff adds no error type. No skill was named under Rules to obey, so none was loaded.

Does not apply. The diff has exactly three `-` lines, all in client.test.ts:2-3 and client.ts:1, and all three are import lines rewritten to add `fetchCoverage`, `RepoCoverage`. No assertion, case or test that already existed is removed, relaxed or rewritten; the eight pre-existing tests are untouched.

The promised behaviour is produced by production code. Reverting the production lines (client.ts:23-26 and types.ts:109-121) leaves `fetchCoverage` non-existent, so both new tests fail to import it. Nothing is hard-coded in the test to stand in for the call: the URL asserted ('/api/coverage') and the field read (`body.coverage`) exist only in client.ts, and the test's stub supplies just the response body a real fetch would.

Nothing beyond the task is written inside the three declared files. types.ts gains only the two vocabularies and the one interface the Contract block asks for; client.ts gains only `fetchCoverage` plus the type import it needs; client.test.ts gains only the two tests **Tests:** names. No refactor, rename, extra helper or adjacent fix, and no `-` line beyond the two rewritten imports. `### Out of scope` names running tests or coverage tools in a clone, reading coverage from CI, history or trend, per-folder coverage, thresholds and colours, and JaCoCo — the diff touches none of them; `CoverageFormat` stays at three members. The Spanish copy and the «Campeones» block, which belong to later tasks of the slice, are not started here.

Two new tests, both with the three properties. Deterministic: no clock, no date, no network, no randomness, no sleep — `fetch` is replaced by `vi.fn()` and the only date is the literal '2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z' inside the fixture. Isolated: each test builds its own `fetchMock` and stubs the global itself before acting, so neither needs state the previous test left nor an order in the file; no file, port or directory is touched. Verifies real behaviour: the first asserts the array `fetchCoverage` returned and the URL the production code requested, the second asserts the `ApiError` and the `code` the production error path produced — both fail if the production lines of this diff are reverted. Nothing outside the three properties is reported, so the test-driven-development skill was not needed.
